purpose: Prochlorperazine is most commonly used to relieve nausea and vomiting, including nausea caused by migraines or surgery. It can also be used to treat anxiety and, less often, symptoms of certain mental health conditions like schizophrenia.
how_it_works: This medication works by blocking certain chemical messengers in your brain, particularly one called dopamine. By blocking these signals, it helps calm the part of your brain that triggers nausea and vomiting. It also has a calming effect on the nervous system, which is why it can help with anxiety.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or dizziness are very common, so be careful when driving or using machinery. You may also notice a dry mouth, blurred vision, or constipation. Some people experience restlessness, muscle stiffness, or unusual muscle movements, especially in the face or neck — let your doctor know right away if this happens.
warnings: This medication can cause a serious condition called tardive dyskinesia, which involves uncontrolled muscle movements, especially with long-term use. It can lower your blood pressure when you stand up quickly, causing lightheadedness. Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine. It is not safe for elderly patients with dementia-related conditions and should be used with caution in children. Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, seizures, or heart issues before taking this medication.
typical_dosing: For nausea and vomiting in adults, the typical dose is 5 to 10 mg taken by mouth 3 to 4 times a day as needed. It can also be given as a suppository (5 or 25 mg) inserted rectally twice a day. Your doctor will adjust the dose based on your condition, so always follow their specific instructions.
